decisions.source_evidence_and_rationale: Both test commands use a throwaway database under the same rule. SQLite by default and --db-url for a real dialect are alternatives within that single setup, not separate actions that require separate presentation.

The dev database is used by migrations validate/lint to clean and replay SQL, by schema apply to rehearse its plan, and by Atlas-compatible verbs for planning, linting, and rollback verification. These distinct command roles need separate retrieval and scope.
The MUSL plus PCRE2 build has one added prerequisite, musl-gcc; its packaging varies by distribution. The qualification belongs with the prerequisite.

The parenthetical makes one installation recommendation about Ubuntu snaps. Malfunctions, resulting bug reports, and maintainer capacity are supporting reasons, not separate user actions or cases that need distinct lookup.

The source expressly calls these two different refusals: MariaDB rejects functional key parts with ERROR 1064, while MySQL permits an index part but rejects a PRIMARY KEY part with ERROR 3756. Engine and key kind must be looked up separately.

The comparison names different folding pairs on MySQL and MariaDB, then adds a distinct MariaDB foreign-key resolution result for the Kelvin pair. Column-name collision and foreign-key binding have different scopes and need separate lookup.

The rule is one early validation of a present invalid environment value. Missing file, unparsable file, and selected environment spelling are examples showing the validation does not depend on document contents.

Both clauses explain the same named-exporter design: existing template rendering removes a need for another evaluator, and declarative structure would introduce another language. They are supporting reasons, with no separate operation or case to retrieve.
The one cache-loading optimization delays remote cache loading until the final matching graph node. The earlier all-vertices condition and final-node behavior are one mechanism.

Definition-based image matching and slower content-based local-source matching are contrasted to explain one solver decision: skip an unnecessary content check and pull. The contrast is necessary to understand the decision as a unit.
The --liquibase-dbms option selects one source database history; keeping matching changesets and reporting excluded ones on standard error are the two outcomes of that single import selection.

The text distinguishes a context selecting an environment from dbms selecting a database, then instructs splitting the changelog along the relevant selector. The two selector scopes need separate presentation for the reader to choose the right split.
